text: 2026 is an extreme drought year. The drought of 2022 motivated me to run for Helix Water District’s Board of Directors, to address water security. I promised water that is pure, healthy, and fairly priced, and I’ve worked to deliver on that promise every day since.

Over these 3-1/2 years, I’ve earned a certificate in Executive Education in Public Policy, attended water conferences, and toured water projects across California to study solutions to our State’s drought challenges. I represent Helix Water District on multiple regional water and infrastructure committees.
My name is Andrea Beth Damsky. I am the current Director of Helix Water District Division 2, asking you to re-elect me for a second term.

Water district directors oversee the district’s finances, water service, and facilities. I fulfill these duties as Chair of our Finance & Administration Committee and our Water Quality & Resources Committee. Every year I’ve served, the District has received a Clean Audit of its financial records.

Next year, the Board will set water rates for the following 5 years, accounting for the rising costs of materials, chemicals, electricity, labor, infrastructure upgrades, and the water itself. This process is strictly regulated by State law: water districts may only charge for the actual cost of providing water. I will hold the line on fairness, as I promised in 2022.

My background is in science: a BS in Environmental Science & Land Use Planning, an MS in Traditional Chinese Medicine, and an Acupuncture License. These disciplines inform my commitment to protecting both our water resources and public health.

I joined this Board after 5 years on La Mesa’s Environmental Sustainability Commission. I proudly supported Helix Water District’s electric vehicle charging project, completed this March. The largest of its kind in California, it meets State electrification mandates, reduces pollution, and was funded 90% by grants, saving our customers the cost.

I also proudly support the East County Advanced Water Purification project, a multi-agency effort in which Helix will provide the final purification phase. Once operational in 2027, ECAWP will supply up to 30% of East County’s water, easing strain on the dwindling Colorado River and building local water independence.
My name is Andrea Beth Damsky. I humbly ask you to re-elect me to the Helix Water District’s Board of Directors, so I can keep this work going for our communities. Thank you.

text: This election presents an important opportunity to lower water rates, bring experienced leadership, practical problem-solving, and responsible long-term planning to the Helix Water District. I am endorsed by 3 of the current board members; Kathleen Coates Hedberg, Board President; Joel A. Scalzitti, Vice President; Dan McMillan, Director. Their endorsement reflects my commitment and knowledge associated with this position.

As your elected representative, I will fight to hold down our water rates. As a family man, I understand the current economic conditions we all face each day and will hold the line on Our Water Rates. Last year, your Board approved an eight point three per cent (8.3%) increase to your water bill; I would have voted NO.

As a business owner responsible for managing multimillion-dollar budgets and large-scale projects, I understand the importance of fiscal responsibility, transparency, and accountability. Public agencies have a duty to carefully manage ratepayer dollars while maintaining the high level of service that residents deserve.

As a volunteer Facility Director for the Mt. Helix Park Foundation, and the former Owner and President of Horizon Homes, Inc., I have spent more than 20 years as a contractor planning, developing, and building residential communities and several infrastructure projects. During that time, I worked closely with water districts, utility providers, engineers, building departments, environmental agencies, and local governments to deliver projects that met the needs of growing communities while protecting valuable public resources. I have navigated complex land use regulations, managed subcontractor procurement and contracts, and overseen project execution while maintaining schedules, budgets, and strategic goals. This work provided a strong understanding of public utility challenges, including rising costs, aging infrastructure, water conservation, and long-term planning. I recognize that prioritizing and implementing critical repairs and capital improvement projects is essential to controlling costs, extending asset life, and ensuring reliable low cost utility operations.

If elected, I will fight to keep water rates low while maintaining safe, reliable infrastructure. I support strategic planning, responsible budgeting, competitive bidding, and thorough contract reviews to maximize value for the public. As a licensed loan officer, I also bring experience securing low-interest financing, to reduce costs and support long-term financial stability.

I am committed to transparency, accountability, and open communication with the community. Please feel free to call me 619-499-4599 or email me at Powers4helixwater@gmail.com if you have any suggestions, comments, or questions.
